goal: Add SimBrief as a second planned-leg import source alongside the existing Little Navmap (.lnmpln) import. The operator saves one SimBrief User ID server-side; clicking "Import from SimBrief" on a trip page fetches their latest OFP/route from SimBrief's API, parses it into the same planned_legs/planned_waypoints/planned_alternates shape the .lnmpln import already produces, and appends it to that trip's planned legs. A failed fetch leaves existing planned legs untouched and shows an actionable message. The .lnmpln path keeps working unchanged.
frozen_decisions: AC1: A visible SimBrief User ID field exists and accepts valid input.
AC2: The SimBrief User ID is stored and prefilled on next app load/session.
AC3: Clicking "Import from SimBrief" triggers a fetch for the latest SimBrief plan for that User ID.
AC4: Imported route legs appear in planned legs without manual re-entry.
AC5: If fetch fails (invalid ID, network/API error, no recent plan), the user sees a clear error message and existing planned legs remain unchanged.
AC6: Little Navmap integration continues to work as before.
Non-functional: reasonable import latency; user-friendly/actionable error states; import success/failure logged for troubleshooting.

The SimBrief User ID field and the "Import from SimBrief" button live inline on client/src/pages/TripDetail.tsx, next to the existing "Import Planned Route (.lnmpln)" section - not a new settings page and not a new route.
One global saved User ID, reused for every trip's import. src/auth/password.ts documents a "single operator account", which confirms this - no multi-user model exists to contradict it.
A NEW small key/value settings table, not a reuse of app_secret (src/db.ts:256-262), whose own doc comment scopes it to server-generated secrets.
The User ID is persisted server-side, never in browser localStorage - the server makes the outbound call.

A new parser module src/simbrief.ts declaring its own ParsedSimbriefPlan type, structurally compatible with db.ts's CreatePlannedLegPlan but not imported from it, wired together in src/server.ts - the same seam the .lnmpln parser uses.
Native Node 20 fetch. No new runtime dependency. The fetch function is injectable (a parameter defaulting to global fetch) so the orchestration logic has a unit-test seam.
The exact SimBrief endpoint, response format and field names are NOT yet verified. Verifying them against the live service is the Designer's job (T-001) and gates every implementation task.
DevOps is skipped for this run: no new dependency, no build/packaging/deploy change expected.
Never touch the running server on port 3000 or the live flights.db. Anything needing a live server uses PORT=3100 against a scratch db copy.
Node 20 via nvm for every command: export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"; . "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"; nvm use 20
No task straddles backend and frontend. Backend: src/**, tests/**, samples/**. Frontend: client/**.
sequencing_rationale: Design comes first and alone gates everything, because the wire format is unverified: endpoint, JSON-vs-XML, field paths and the "no recent plan" signal all shape the parser type, the error taxonomy and the UI states. This mirrors the XSD-verification gate the 2026-09-04-lnmpln-trip-planner run put ahead of its parser task.

Phase 1 ships persistence only (AC1, AC2). Storing and prefilling the ID is independently useful and independently falsifiable, and it isolates the one schema change in the run behind its own review gate before any outbound network code exists.
Phase 2 ships the import itself (AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6) on top of a setting already proven durable.

The risky part is split into two modules with a CLI inspector: src/simbrief.ts is pure (parse only - no network, no db) and src/simbriefClient.ts owns the network behind an injectable fetch. Both are falsifiable by npm test with no network, and by npx ts-node src/inspect-simbrief.ts against committed fixtures, without the sim and without a live server.

SimBrief gets a SIBLING route; the existing multer-backed POST /api/trips/:id/planned-legs handler is not modified. AC6 is then protected structurally rather than by care, and every task carries a git-diff criterion that says so.

src/server.ts is touched by T-002 and T-006, and client/src/pages/TripDetail.tsx by T-003 and T-007. Those pairs sit in different phases on purpose: the phase-1 reviewer gate (T-004) is the mechanism that stops them ever running concurrently. Nothing inside a phase shares a path.

T-005 and T-006 are consecutive backend_sr tasks on one dependency chain and should go to a single implementer agent, batched - they are split here only because their verification modes differ (hermetic unit tests and a CLI inspector versus a scratch server and curl), which makes the review verdicts separable.

No DevOps task: native fetch adds no dependency, and if design wants a base-URL override for end-to-end verification it must read it in the SimBrief module itself (the EXPORT_BASE_URL precedent at src/pdfExport.ts:28), not in src/config.ts - src/config.ts owns security-relevant env only, and its ENV_VARS list is asserted by tests/config.test.ts.

tasks.title: Verify SimBrief's real API and freeze the whole contract
tasks.goal: Fetch SimBrief's API for real, record what it actually returns, and freeze design.md as eight numbered sections covering: the verified API, the settings table, the settings endpoints, ParsedSimbriefPlan and its mapping onto db.ts's CreatePlannedLegPlan, the fetch client and error taxonomy, the import endpoint, the client contract plus the end-to-end verification recipe, and the .lnmpln surfaces that must not change. No code is written in this task.
acceptance_criteria: A real, unedited SimBrief response is saved under .claude/runs/2026-09-13-simbrief-import/contracts/ with the exact request URL and fetch date recorded next to it. If no response can be obtained without the operator's own account, return blocked naming exactly what is needed (a User ID to test with, or a saved OFP export file) - do not design against a remembered or documented shape.

design.md section 1 states, citing the captured sample and the URL it came from, the endpoint, its query parameters, whether the response is JSON or XML, whether any auth is needed, and the literal field paths for: departure ICAO, destination ICAO, the en-route waypoint list (ident, lat, lon, altitude, airway/type), alternates, cruise altitude, aircraft type, flight rules, OFP id and generation time. Every claim names the line of the sample it came from.

Section 1 also states how "unknown user id" and "no recent plan" are signalled - HTTP status, body shape, literal error string - quoted from actual failing requests made during this task, not inferred.

Section 2 freezes the settings table: DDL, column names, where it goes inside the existing CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS block in src/db.ts, the accessor signatures, and one sentence on why app_secret is not reused.

Section 3 freezes the settings endpoints: method and path for read and write, request and response JSON, the validation rule for a SimBrief User ID (character set, length, trimming, case), and the status plus body for every rejection.

Section 4 freezes ParsedSimbriefPlan field by field and its mapping onto CreatePlannedLegPlan (src/db.ts:767-851): which SimBrief field feeds which, which CreatePlannedLegPlan fields have no SimBrief source and what value they take instead, and what source_filename and source_sha256 hold for a non-file import (planned_legs declares both NOT NULL, src/db.ts:187-188). State explicitly whether re-importing the same OFP is detectable via findPlannedLegBySource's (trip_id, source_sha256) key, given that two fetches of the same plan may not be byte-identical.

Section 5 freezes the fetch client: the exported signature including the injectable fetch parameter and its default, the timeout, and a complete error taxonomy - code, log line format, user-facing message - covering at least unknown/invalid user id, no recent plan, network failure, non-200 status, and an unparseable body.

Section 6 freezes the import endpoint: method and path (a sibling route - the existing POST /api/trips/:id/planned-legs is not modified), request body, success and failure response shapes, duplicate handling, and the guarantee that a failed import writes nothing at all.

Section 7 freezes the client contract - the types added to client/src/types.ts, where the field and button sit on TripDetail.tsx, every state rendered - AND the end-to-end verification recipe: precisely how an implementer exercises a SUCCESSFUL import on PORT=3100 against a scratch db copy without the operator's SimBrief account. If that needs a base-URL override, it is read inside the SimBrief module itself, following the EXPORT_BASE_URL precedent at src/pdfExport.ts:28, never added to src/config.ts's ENV_VARS.
Section 8 lists the .lnmpln surfaces that must stay unchanged, by file and line range, so each later task can assert it with git diff.

Every heading is of the form '## <n>. <title>' so that .claude/tools/ctx.sh design 2026-09-13-simbrief-import <n> returns exactly that one section. Run it for each of 1 through 8 and paste the first line of each result.
